hypothesis: After a link-loss indication an idle OPEN session reports LOST without fault, keeps its socket, admits only the same network and recovers through reassociation.
conclusion: Loss recovery behaved as designed on the host model; firmware key and port state after a disconnection indication has not been observed on hardware.
narrative: checks/radio-recovery-loss.c, built and run with checks/radio-reconnect.py --fixture loss (both removed from the repository as one-off radio compositions), executed the actual session, network adapter, socket service and IP task on the modeled MMIO of the reconnect composition. An idle fixed-address OPEN association with one open UDP socket received a source-layout disconnection indication. The session reported LOST without fault, the network was offline, and submissions were refused while the socket survived. Recovery refused another SSID, another security mode, a channel outside the admitted list, missing beacon evidence and missing OPEN authority. It admitted a second access point of the same network with its own BSSID and beacon evidence; its first reassociation failed in the indication and the retry associated with that access point at association generation three. Received frames then carried the new BSSID, and the address and a new TCP exchange followed. A separate part of the same image retired a WPA2 security pair after loss: no port command, the pairwise key wiped locally, one group-key KEY_DEL with its hardware index, and rearm accepted for a later generation. Key state there was a modeled input, and the WPA2 handshake after recovery was not executed.

hypothesis: A requested reconnect disposes the old sockets and handle, rearms the session and supports a new TCP exchange; rearm is refused with a live key, fault or attached worker.
narrative: The AArch64 composition in checks/radio-reconnect.c (removed) passed once with actual FreeRTOS tasks, providers, session workers, disconnect and connect parsing, socket disposal, an IP-task FIFO receipt and a new TCP exchange. It refused expired admission, unread replies and live sockets, then rejected the disposed old handle after reconnect. Separate cases in that image refused rearm with a live key, fault or attached worker and exercised fresh RSN creation and controlled-port retirement without resetting the data sequence; their initial retired pair is modeled. The OPEN composition links the board owner wrapper without executing it.

hypothesis: The board_radio_reconnect wrapper and session polling restore a WPA2 session with a fresh four-way handshake, new keys and a new TCP exchange.
conclusion: The WPA2 reconnect sequence completed on the host model; physical reconnection is unqualified.
narrative: The WPA2 composition in checks/radio-reconnect-wpa.c (removed) executed the actual board_radio_reconnect wrapper and session polling. Preserved terminal RAM shows confirmed old port closure, two key deletions, detach, disconnect, reassociation, fresh RSN rearm, M1-M4 processing against cached peer vectors, two new keys and port authorization, generation-two address restoration and a new TCP exchange. The client suspended only after its successful receive and CLOSE assertions, and the borrowed generation equals the retained platform clock token. The fixture reached its loop assertion because its readiness publication overwrote the client's completion value, and emitted no PASS; completion was verified from the saved terminal RAM, exact executable and client suspension. The corrected reporting source was not executed. Earlier vector-format setup and request-after-poll refusals remained preserved. Four distinct linked images cover the OPEN result and the WPA2 attempts; the 101 production objects were reused unchanged for each WPA2 image. Frozen inputs, images, attempt history and terminal classification are under the evidence directory. Board startup and board_radio_poll were not executed; firmware upload, initial association and the old authorized security state are explicit modeled checkpoints, and register, peer firmware, entropy and RF effects were modeled.
